rule: All resolved places remain selectable with a score; only independently audited settlements scoring 60 or more appear as town markers.

additions.name: Tayport
additions.rationale: A substantial harbour and coastal town requiring a complete independent audit before its map score is published.

additions.name: Leuchars
additions.rationale: The village, rather than the railway station alone, is the assessment subject; heritage and visitor depth must be checked independently.

additions.name: Guardbridge
additions.rationale: Industrial heritage and estuary access are relevant, but nearby St Andrews and Eden attractions are not transferred automatically.

additions.name: Rhynd
additions.rationale: The mapped farm and any destination business are kept distinct from settlement-level visitor merit.

additions.name: Carrick
additions.rationale: The historic Fife place-name at NO441226 is retained without inheriting Leuchars or Tayport attractions.
additions.resolutionNote: Resolved from the Fife Place-name Data grid reference NO441226.

additions.name: Kincaple
additions.rationale: Kincaple is assessed on its own compact fabric and services, not on nearby St Andrews.

additions.name: Strathkinness
additions.rationale: A coherent village that needs its own See, daytime food, trail and practical-facility evidence checked before crossing 60.

additions.name: Newpark
additions.rationale: Newpark is treated as a named St Andrews locality around New Park Place and the former New Park estate, not as an independent town.
additions.resolutionNote: Resolved to the Newpark locality recorded beside New Mill and modern New Park Place.

additions.name: Balone
additions.rationale: Balone remains a regional reference and does not inherit St Andrews or Craigtoun visitor value.

additions.name: Denhead
additions.rationale: The hamlet is assessed independently from Mount Melville, Peat Inn and St Andrews attractions.

additions.name: Peat Inn
additions.rationale: A notable restaurant is assessed under Eat but cannot by itself turn the hamlet into a tourist town.

additions.name: St Andrews
additions.rationale: A major destination deliberately held below publication until its unusually large heritage and visitor dataset passes the complete audit.

additions.name: Brownhills
additions.rationale: Brownhills is a named rural locality rather than a visitor settlement and does not inherit St Andrews attractions.

additions.name: Boarhills
additions.rationale: Church, landscape and walking evidence require checking without transferring nearby coast or estate attractions into the hamlet score.

additions.name: Kingsbarns
additions.rationale: The village, beach, golf and nearby estate/distillery relationships require strict boundary separation before a final score is published.
additions.resolutionNote: The requested spelling is normalised to Kingsbarns.

additions.name: Prior Muir
additions.rationale: Prior Muir remains selectable but does not inherit St Andrews, Dunino or coastal attractions.

additions.name: Stravithie
additions.rationale: The surviving rural locality is separated from the wider medieval lands and vanished castle site when scoring a visit.
additions.resolutionNote: The requested spelling is normalised to Stravithie.

additions.name: Dunino
additions.rationale: The kirk, den and related heritage may support a specialist stop, but the hamlet must pass the complete facilities and boundary audit first.

additions.name: Balcomie
additions.rationale: Balcomie is retained as a locality; the golf links, beach and castle are separate attractions and cannot manufacture a town score.

additions.name: Craighead
additions.rationale: Craighead at NO632098 is retained without treating Craighead Links or the Fife Ness coast as a settlement offer.
additions.resolutionNote: Resolved from the Fife Place-name Data grid reference NO632098.
